fruit_state: The cross-section is rounded rather than sharply angular.
source_text: Harvest export bunches at the compact three-quarter stage. Fingers should be filled out, with softened ridges and a rounded cross-section rather than sharp angles. In warm lowland blocks, this stage is usually reached 12–13 weeks after bunch emergence; cooler blocks may require 14–15 weeks. Do not wait for yellow peel. Cut with 8–10 cm of stalk and lower each bunch onto a padded support. Wash off latex, allow fruit to dry, grade, and pack in ventilated cartons. Hold packed fruit at 13–14 °C.
harvest_decision: Harvest when the bunch reaches the compact three-quarter stage; use the stated age ranges as a guide and do not wait for yellow peel.

Mature fingers have rounded shoulders and reduced angularity.
The bunch surface is dry at cutting.
source_text: For hand-ripened supply, harvest a bunch only when median fingers on the second hand measure at least 30 mm across at the midpoint. Mature fingers have rounded shoulders and reduced angularity. Bunches are normally ready about 11 weeks after flowering; fruit cut before 10 weeks often shrivels before ripening. Cut in the early morning only when the bunch surface is dry; postpone work during rain. After cutting, separate the hands, let latex drain for 15 minutes in clean water, and sanitize knives between bunches. Pre-cool packed hands to 14 °C.
harvest_decision: Harvest when the median fingers on the second hand are at least 30 mm in diameter and the bunch is normally around 11 weeks after flowering. Avoid cutting before 10 weeks, and postpone work during rain or while the bunch surface is wet.

fruit_state: The peel is uniformly dark green.
Ridges are nearly absent on harvest-ready fingers.
Bunches with prominent angular fingers are not yet ready for cutting.
source_text: Where green bananas must travel for up to five days, select bunches at 12–13 weeks after flowering. At cutting, the peel should be uniformly dark green and fingers fully filled, with the ridges nearly absent; leave bunches with prominent angular fingers on the plant. Harvest after dew has dried and keep cut bunches shaded. Remove damaged fingers during grading, use clean ventilated crates, and maintain 13–14 °C in storage; temperatures below 12 °C can cause chilling injury.
